add.title: Transgender rights in the United States — Wikipedia (federal prison-placement rule + August 2022 Nebraska ruling)
add.summary: Wikipedia: under the January 2017 Obama-era Bureau of Prisons guidelines trans prisoners could be transferred to facilities of the gender they identify with, but on May 11 2018 the BOP rescinded the guidelines so that assigned sex at birth once again determines where trans prisoners are jailed; it then documents the Nebraska-specific case: in August 2022 a federal judge in Nebraska ruled against a transgender woman who had been denied gender-affirming care in prison and placed in a cell with a male sex offender who sexually assaulted her, holding there was insufficient evidence of deliberate indifference to her gender dysphoria and that she had not proven more than minimal injuries from the assault, finding no support that a substantial risk could be inferred from a prospective cellmate's sexual-offence conviction 'coupled with the alleged vulnerability of a transgender inmate transitioning to a woman in a men's prison'. Confirms Nebraska practices birth-sex (men's prison) placement and that the placement followed her there.

add.title: Transgender inmate loses lawsuit over prison's treatment for her gender dysphoria — Lori Pilger, Lincoln Journal Star (via Norfolk Daily News, archived)
add.summary: Lincoln Journal Star (Lori Pilger, Aug 10 2022, updated Aug 11 2022; archived by the Wayback Machine after the original page went dead): U.S. District Judge Brian C. Buescher ruled for Nebraska prison officials and workers sued by a transgender inmate identified only as 'Jane Doe', who was diagnosed with gender dysphoria and transitioning to be a woman while held in Nebraska's men's prison. The judge dismissed her claims of failure to treat her dysphoria, denial of gender-conforming surgery, and failure to protect her: he previously dismissed the claim that guards failed to protect her after she was placed in a cell with a convicted sex offender who victimized her, wrote that 'without medical evidence, no reasonable jury could conclude that the providers were deliberately indifferent to Doe's serious medical need', and said she had not plausibly alleged more than de minimis injuries from the assault. Primary news documentation that Nebraska housed her by assigned birth sex among male prisoners and celled her with a male sex offender.
